recipes.name: Gingered Carrot Soup
ingredients_raw: 4 cups Kitchen Basics® Original or Unsalted Chicken Stock
0.5 cup evaporated milk (or for an alternative with less fat, use half and half)
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in heavy large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add onion, ginger, and garlic; sauté until onion is translucent, about 8 minutes. Add stock and carrots; cover and simmer until carrots are tender, about 30 minutes.

Fill blender or the bowl of a food processor halfway with soup. Cover and hold lid down with a potholder; pulse a few times before leaving on to blend. Pour into a saucepan. Repeat with remaining soup.
Heat soup over low heat; stir in evaporated milk and cumin. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Gingered Carrot Soup
raw_recipe.description: Infused with lots of grated fresh ginger and a hint of garlic, this creamy gingered carrot soup recipe makes the perfect start to a fall lunch or dinner.

review.reviewBody: Great soup alternative for a cool fall night. I noticed the ingredient list shows 4 cups chicken stock but directions call for only 3 cups. I used 3 and the soup came out creamy...just right. I didn't have cumin but substituted rosemary..worked fine.

I used this recipe as a starting point, and then like so many others, adapted it to make it right for our family. I made a lower calorie version of this recipe. I sliced and peeled 7 lbs of carrots and 2 large onions. I boiled these in 4 quarts of vegetable broth, along with a medium sized piece of fresh ginger that I shredded into the pot. I just wanted a hit of ginger in my soup, so I'd say I only used about 1/4-1/3 cup of ginger for the entire batch. When the vegetables were soft, I used my immersable blender to make everything pureed. Then I added about a quart of fat free half and half. This can be as thick or thin as you like by using more or less veggie broth. Salt and pepper to taste. It was delicious and perfect as is, or add a dollop of sour cream and a few croutons if you don't mind the extra calories.

I made this and it is delicious! I used carrots, celery, fresh ginger and fresh minced garlic AND 1 gold yukon potato. I added Chicken Bone Broth and blended it in my Vitamix Blender and did not add any cream. I could have, but wanted to have a healthier option so I can have a glass of wine and some chicharrones with it! ha!

My family all loved it. The flavor profile is really nice. For personal preference, I used red onion, doubled the garlic and halved the ginger. Sautéed the onions in the oil on their own and only added the garlic and ginger for the last minute of sautéing. Used canned coconut milk in place of evap. Delicious!

This is a delicious soup! But be sure you like ginger, because it definitely packs a good ginger punch! I went with grating the ginger and used the amount called for. Also I used 3 cups stock and half and half. I think it would be just as good with low fat milk. I pureed it with my immersion blender, seasoned it with some salt, and presto! Delicious, spicy, flavorful soup! Today for lunch, I topped it with a dollop of fat free greek yogurt. YUM!

I made this soup for two servings instead of four by halving all ingredients and it turned out as good as the original 4 servings which I made before. I noticed the ingredients list calls for 4 cups of chicken stock but the instruction says add 3 cups. So I went with the 3 cup version because you can always more. 3 cups was perfectly enough and yield the desired thickness.

Very good soup! I doubled the batch and am super glad I did. In a double batch I used 1 cup less water (7cups total) and a bit extra evaporated milk so I could use the whole can (354mL). I also added a bit extra ginger as it was cooking because it didn’t smell like it had quite enough and a couple tbspns of brown sugar after it was puréed. Will definitely be using this recipe for my surplus of carrots from the garden in the future!

Excellent Flavor :-). 
I use ginger in a lot of my recipes and juices, so recently I've been running my ginger thru a juicer, then freezing it in an ice cube tray and then place them in a ziploc bag. 
So with this in mind, I used 1.5 cubes of ginger, and I replaced the chicken broth with vegetable broth and 4 cups of carrots instead of the 3 mentioned. This has most definitely become another favorite. Thank you, allrecipes.com!

I'll make it again. Next time I'll add sweet potatoes or apples to give it a little sweeter flavor and I'll puree it longer (I still had some little bits, would have liked it more smoothed out.)

The carrots I used may have been a little old or something b/c the soup tasted kind of bitter. I added some orange juice and cinnamon and that helped.

The comments about using the amount of broth mentioned in the directions as opposed to the amount in the ingredient list were helpful. I also used about half as much ginger and it still had plenty of ginger taste.

This was AH-MAZ-ING! I think where I had success in the “thickness” was I cooked in my cast iron pot. I used 4c broth and it cooked down. I used condensed milk and my immersion blender and this was thick and wonderful and oh so delicious!! The only change was using Trader Joe’s frozen ginger cubes - which was minced and a total of 3 cubes. Minus peeling four cups of carrots, this was super easy! Would highly recommend and will make again!! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe Kitchen Basics!!

I doubled the ingredients to be able to make enough to carry over for a couple of meals. Freshly grated ginger is key even if a labor of love. To see all of my kids absolutely love the soup and say it tasted exotic and finish it was a treat! We added parsley prior to serving and a dollop of sour cream to individual bowls to balance the spice of the ginger. That was also delightful. We will make it again! Thank you!

I forgot to purchase fresh ginger so I substituted with ground ginger. This may be one reason it didn’t have much flavor. I added more salt & pepper and ginger. Still not enough. I ended up adding leftovers- an edamame, corn & onion dish- and it was great!
Easy and delicious. I used vegetable stock
Excellent and 'easy' to make soup. We substituted the ½ cup evaporated milk for low fat coconut milk. Pairs well with the ginger.

A terrific soup, especially for a cooler fall night or cold winter day. I'm giving it four stars because unless you like your soup really watery, there's no need for 4 cups of chicken broth. Start with two cups and add more to get the consistency that you want. Also, no one wanted to eat it with that much ginger. I had to use about 1/4 cup minus 1 tablespoon before the sharpness of the ginger didn't overwhelm the flavor.

Simple yet fancy. Love all the fresh ingredients that are easy to find and cheap.
I added some white miso also for some umami. Garnished with sour cream and cilantro.
Not to my taste - very thin, not creamy. Almost like a broth with very little flavor. I won’t make it again.
